chapter: Miles Davis band and Kind of Blue
title: Washington bassists and the Warren family
summary: Brower asks about Marshall Hawkins, Butch Warren and Quentin Warren.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you know the name Marshall Hawkins?
I heard somewhere that was – might have been in line to get Ron’s slot, what became Ron Carter’s slot.
He could have been. He’s a pretty good bass player. What about the other boy that was with Monk?
Butch Warren. Butch Warren was a good bass player.
Did you know the family, Eddie Warren?
I knew his daddy. Piano player, right?
I played some gigs with him, I think.
Yeah, when Butch was a young boy.

Yeah. I knew them guys. Washington was okay back then. It was kind of busy. You could see somebody come into town every week at all them different little places they had, the theater, and the – what is it? – Benghazi or whatever that stuff was. It was a few little places that . . .
You had 7th Street, 9th Street, 14th Street, and U Street, all those . . .
Yeah, all those places had some music going on.
